note: Questions from the CBSE Class XII Physics board exam 2023, Q.P. code 55/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. Q2, whose options are graphs, is left out; other figures are described in words. Solutions are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A point charge situated at a distance r from a short electric dipole on its axis experiences a force F. If the distance of the charge is 2r, the force on the charge will be :
questions.solution: The axial field of a short dipole varies as 1/r³, so doubling r divides the force by 8.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The potential difference across a cell in an open circuit is 8 V. It falls to 4 V when a current of 4 A is drawn from it. The internal resistance of the cell is :
questions.solution: E = 8 V. V = E − Ir: 4 = 8 − 4r, so r = 1 Ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A steady current flows through a metallic wire whose area of cross-section A increases continuously from one end of the wire to the other. How does the magnitude of the drift velocity v_d of the free electrons vary with A?
options: v_d decreases as A increases, varying as 1/A (a rectangular hyperbola)
v_d stays constant as A increases
questions.solution: I = neAv_d is the same everywhere along the wire, so v_d = I/(neA) ∝ 1/A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A diamagnetic substance is brought near the north or south pole of a bar magnet. It will be :
options: repelled by the north pole and attracted by the south pole.
attracted by the north pole and repelled by the south pole.
questions.solution: Diamagnetic substances move from stronger to weaker field regions, so either pole repels them.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A circular coil of radius 8.0 cm and 40 turns is rotated about its vertical diameter with an angular speed of 25/π rad s⁻¹ in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of magnitude 3.0 × 10⁻² T. The maximum emf induced in the coil is :

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A rectangular conductor PSRQ has a movable arm PQ of length l and resistance r; the resistance of the rest of the frame is negligible. The frame lies in a uniform magnetic field B perpendicular to its plane, and PQ is moved with velocity v. The magnitude of the emf induced does not depend on :
questions.solution: Motional emf ε = Blv does not depend on the resistance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In the process of charging a capacitor, the current produced between the plates of the capacitor is :
questions.solution: The displacement current is I_d = ε₀ dΦ_E/dt.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For a concave mirror of focal length f, the minimum distance between the object and its real image is :
questions.solution: When the object is at the centre of curvature (2f), the real image forms at the same place, so the distance is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The radius of the nth orbit in the Bohr model of the hydrogen atom is proportional to :
questions.solution: rₙ = n²r₁.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A hydrogen atom initially in the ground state absorbs a photon which excites it to the n = 5 level. The wavelength of the photon is :

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The mass density of a nucleus of mass number A is :
questions.solution: Mass ∝ A and volume ∝ R³ ∝ A, so the density is independent of A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An ac source of voltage is connected in series with a p-n junction diode and a load resistor. The output voltage across the load resistance will be :
options: the full sine wave, both halves
positive half-cycles on every half cycle (full-wave rectified)
positive half-cycles only, with gaps in between (half-wave rectified)
questions.solution: A single diode conducts only in alternate half cycles, giving half-wave rectified output.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: When an intrinsic semiconductor is doped with a small amount of trivalent impurity, then :
options: there will be more free electrons than holes in the semiconductor.
questions.solution: Trivalent atoms accept electrons, creating holes: the material becomes p-type (and its resistance decreases).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In the energy-band diagram of n-type Si, the gap between the bottom of the conduction band E_C and the donor energy level E_D is of the order of :
questions.solution: Donor levels lie very close below the conduction band, about 0.01 to 0.05 eV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): When a bar of copper is placed in an external magnetic field, the field lines get concentrated inside the bar.
Reason (R): Copper is a paramagnetic substance.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.
questions.solution: Copper is diamagnetic, so field lines are pushed out of it, not concentrated. Both A and R are false.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The phase difference between any two points on a wavefront is zero.
Reason (R): All points on a wavefront are at the same distance from the source and thus oscillate in the same phase.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.
questions.solution: A wavefront is a surface of constant phase, which is why the phase difference is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.text:
Assertion (A): The photoelectric effect demonstrates the particle nature of light.
Reason (R): Photoelectric current is proportional to the intensity of incident radiation for frequencies more than the threshold frequency.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.
questions.solution: Both are true, but the particle nature is shown by the threshold frequency and the instant emission, not by current ∝ intensity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An alpha particle is projected with velocity v = (3.0 × 10⁵ m/s) î into a region in which the magnetic field B = (0.4 T) î + (0.3 T) ĵ exists. Calculate the acceleration of the particle in the region. The charge to mass ratio of the alpha particle is 4.8 × 10⁷ C/kg.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Consider an induced magnetic field due to a changing electric field and an induced electric field due to a changing magnetic field. Which one is more easily observed? Justify your answer.
questions.solution: The induced electric field (electromagnetic induction) is far easier to observe. The induced magnetic field from displacement current, ε₀μ₀ dΦ_E/dt, has the factor 1/c², so it is extremely small unless the electric field changes very rapidly.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Using Huygens' principle, draw a ray diagram showing the propagation of a plane wave refracting at a plane surface separating two media. Also verify Snell's law of refraction.
questions.solution: Let wavefront AB be incident at angle i. While the disturbance at B travels BC = v₁t to the surface, the secondary wavelet from A travels AE = v₂t in medium 2. The tangent CE is the refracted wavefront, at angle r. In triangles ABC and AEC: sin i = v₁t/AC and sin r = v₂t/AC. So sin i/sin r = v₁/v₂ = n₂/n₁, which is Snell's law.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Why is a reflecting telescope preferred over a refracting telescope? Justify your answer giving two reasons.
questions.solution: A mirror has no chromatic aberration; a parabolic mirror avoids spherical aberration; a large mirror is lighter and cheaper than an equally large lens and can be supported over its whole back, so a bigger aperture (more light, better resolution) is possible.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Two coherent monochromatic light beams of intensities I and 4I superpose each other. Find the ratio of maximum and minimum intensities in the resulting beam.
questions.solution: Amplitudes are in the ratio 1 : 2. I_max ∝ (1 + 2)² = 9, I_min ∝ (2 − 1)² = 1. Ratio 9 : 1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The ground state energy of the hydrogen atom is −13.6 eV. What are the potential energy and kinetic energy of an electron in the third excited state?
questions.solution: The third excited state is n = 4: E = −13.6/16 = −0.85 eV. KE = −E = 0.85 eV and PE = 2E = −1.7 eV.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Differentiate between intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductors.
questions.solution: Intrinsic: a pure semiconductor; numbers of free electrons and holes are equal; low conductivity that depends mainly on temperature. Extrinsic: doped with impurity atoms; electrons and holes are unequal (n-type or p-type); much higher conductivity that can be controlled by the doping level.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Draw the circuit arrangement for studying the V-I characteristics of a p-n junction diode in forward bias and reverse bias. Show the plot of the V-I characteristic of a silicon diode.
questions.solution: Forward bias: battery with a potential divider, the diode's p-side to the positive terminal, a milliammeter in series and a voltmeter across the diode. Reverse bias: battery reversed, with a microammeter. Plot: forward current is nearly zero up to about 0.7 V, then rises steeply; reverse current is tiny (μA) and nearly constant until breakdown, where it rises sharply.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Briefly explain how the diffusion and drift currents contribute to the formation of the potential barrier in a p-n junction diode.
questions.solution: Electrons diffuse from n to p and holes from p to n (diffusion current), leaving immobile positive ions on the n-side and negative ions on the p-side. These ions set up an electric field (barrier potential) that drives minority carriers back across (drift current). The barrier grows until drift equals diffusion and the net current is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(a) Twelve negative charges of the same magnitude q are equally spaced and fixed on the circumference of a circle of radius R. Relative to potential being zero at infinity, find the electric potential and electric field at the centre C of the circle.
(b) If the same charges are unequally spaced and fixed on an arc of 120° of radius R, find the electric potential at the centre C.
questions.solution: (a) V = 12 × (−kq/R) = −12q/(4πε₀R). The fields of diametrically opposite charges cancel, so E = 0. (b) Each charge is still at distance R, and potential is a scalar, so V = −12q/(4πε₀R) again.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: How does resistance differ from impedance? With the help of a suitable phasor diagram, obtain an expression for the impedance of a series LCR circuit connected to a source v = v_m sin ωt.
questions.solution: Resistance opposes current in both dc and ac and does not depend on frequency; impedance is the total opposition in an ac circuit, combining resistance with inductive and capacitive reactances, which depend on frequency. Phasors: V_R along the current, V_L 90° ahead, V_C 90° behind. v_m² = V_R² + (V_C − V_L)² = i_m²[R² + (X_C − X_L)²], so Z = √(R² + (X_C − X_L)²).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Find the condition for resonance in a series LCR circuit connected to a source v = v_m sin ωt, where ω can be varied. Give the factors on which the resonant frequency of a series LCR circuit depends. Plot a graph showing the variation of electric current with frequency in a series LCR circuit.
questions.solution: Current is maximum when Z is minimum, i.e. X_L = X_C: ω₀L = 1/(ω₀C), ω₀ = 1/√(LC). The resonant frequency depends only on L and C. Graph: current rises to a peak at ω₀ and falls on either side; the peak is sharper for smaller R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A long solenoid of radius r consists of n turns per unit length. A current I = I₀ sin ωt flows in the solenoid. A coil of N turns is wound tightly around it near its centre. What is (a) the induced emf in the coil? (b) the mutual inductance between the solenoid and the coil?
questions.solution: Flux through the coil Φ = N μ₀ n I πr². (a) ε = −dΦ/dt = −μ₀nNπr²I₀ω cos ωt. (b) M = Φ/I = μ₀nNπr².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.text: How does Einstein's photoelectric equation explain the emission of electrons from a metal surface? Explain briefly. Plot the variation of photocurrent with (a) collector plate potential for different intensities of incident radiation, and (b) intensity of incident radiation.
questions.solution: Kmax = hν − φ₀: a photon gives all its energy hν to one electron; part (φ₀) frees it and the rest is kinetic energy. Emission needs ν > ν₀ = φ₀/h, Kmax grows linearly with ν, and the number of electrons (current) grows with intensity. (a) Current rises with collector potential to a saturation value, higher for greater intensity; all curves fall to zero at the same stopping potential. (b) A straight line through the origin: photocurrent ∝ intensity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Draw the energy level diagram for the hydrogen atom. Mark the transitions corresponding to the series lying in the ultraviolet region, visible region and infrared region.
questions.solution: Levels Eₙ = −13.6/n² eV: −13.6, −3.4, −1.51, −0.85, … converging to 0. Lyman series (to n = 1): ultraviolet. Balmer series (to n = 2): visible. Paschen (to n = 3), Brackett (to n = 4) and Pfund (to n = 5): infrared.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Draw a diagram to show the variation of binding energy per nucleon with mass number for different nuclei and mention its two features. Why do lighter nuclei usually undergo nuclear fusion?
questions.solution: BE/A rises steeply for light nuclei, peaks at about 8.75 MeV near A = 56 and decreases slowly to about 7.6 MeV for A ≈ 238. Features: BE/A is nearly constant (about 8 MeV) for 30 < A < 170, showing the nuclear force saturates; lower BE/A for heavy nuclei explains fission, and for light nuclei explains fusion. Light nuclei fuse because the product has higher BE/A, so energy is released.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(i) State Coulomb's law in electrostatics and write it in vector form for two charges.
(ii) 'Gauss's law is based on the inverse-square dependence on distance contained in Coulomb's law.' Explain.
(iii) Two charges A (charge q) and B (charge 2q) are located at points (0, 0) and (a, a) respectively. Let î and ĵ be the unit vectors along the x-axis and y-axis. Find the force exerted by A on B, in terms of î and ĵ.
questions.solution: (i) The force between two point charges is proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them, along the line joining them: F₂₁ = (1/4πε₀)(q₁q₂/r²) r̂₂₁. (ii) For a point charge, E ∝ 1/r² and the area of a sphere ∝ r², so the flux q/ε₀ is independent of r; this only works because of the inverse-square law. (iii) r = a î + a ĵ, |r| = √2 a. F = k(2q²)/(2a²) × (î + ĵ)/√2 = (q²/(4√2 πε₀a²))(î + ĵ).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(i) Derive an expression for the electric field at a point on the equatorial plane of an electric dipole consisting of charges q and −q separated by a distance 2a.
(ii) The distance of a far off point on the equatorial plane of an electric dipole is halved. How will the electric field be affected?
(iii) Two identical electric dipoles are placed along the diagonals of a square ABCD of side √2 m: charges +q at A (top left), −q at B (top right), −q at C (bottom right) and +q at D (bottom left), so one dipole is A–C and the other D–B. Obtain the magnitude and direction of the net electric field at the centre O of the square.
questions.solution: (i) Each charge is at distance √(r² + a²) and gives kq/(r² + a²). The components perpendicular to the axis cancel; those along the axis add: E = 2kqa/(r² + a²)^(3/2) = kp/(r² + a²)^(3/2), opposite to p. (ii) For r ≫ a, E ∝ 1/r³, so halving r makes the field 8 times. (iii) Each corner is 1 m from O. Along AC, +q at A and −q at C both give kq towards C: 2kq towards C. Along DB: 2kq towards B. These are perpendicular, so E = 2√2 kq = 2√2 × 9 × 10⁹ q ≈ 2.5 × 10¹⁰ q N/C, directed parallel to AB from side AD towards side BC.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(i) State the Biot-Savart law for the magnetic field due to a current carrying element. Use this law to obtain an expression for the magnetic field at the centre of a circular loop of radius a carrying a current I. Draw the magnetic field lines for a current loop indicating the direction of the magnetic field.
(ii) An electron is revolving around the nucleus in a circular orbit with a speed of 10⁷ m s⁻¹. If the radius of the orbit is 10⁻¹⁰ m, find the current constituted by the revolving electron in the orbit.
questions.solution: (i) dB = (μ₀/4π) I dl × r̂/r². At the centre every element is perpendicular to the radius a and gives a field along the axis: B = (μ₀I/4πa²) ∮dl = μ₀I/(2a). The field lines pass through the loop along the axis and close around the wire (direction by the right-hand rule), like a bar magnet's. (ii) T = 2πr/v = 2π × 10⁻¹⁰/10⁷ = 2π × 10⁻¹⁷ s. I = e/T = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹/(6.28 × 10⁻¹⁷) ≈ 2.5 × 10⁻³ A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(i) Derive an expression for the force acting on a current carrying straight conductor kept in a magnetic field. State the rule which is used to find the direction of this force. Give the condition under which this force is (1) maximum, and (2) minimum.
(ii) Two long parallel straight wires A and B are 2.5 cm apart in air. They carry 5.0 A and 2.5 A currents respectively in opposite directions. Calculate the magnitude of the force exerted by wire A on a 10 cm length of wire B.
questions.solution: (i) A conductor of length l and area A has nAl electrons with drift velocity v_d; each feels −e v_d × B. Total F = (nAl)(−e v_d × B) = I l × B, magnitude IlB sin θ. Direction by Fleming's left-hand rule. (1) Maximum (IlB) when the conductor is perpendicular to B; (2) zero when parallel. (ii) F = μ₀I₁I₂l/(2πd) = 2 × 10⁻⁷ × 5 × 2.5 × 0.1/0.025 = 1 × 10⁻⁵ N (repulsive).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(i) (1) Write two points of difference between an interference pattern and a diffraction pattern. (2) Name any two factors on which the fringe width in a Young's double-slit experiment depends.
(ii) In Young's double-slit experiment, the two slits are separated by a distance equal to 100 times the wavelength of the light passing through the slits. Calculate (1) the angular separation in radians between the central maximum and the adjacent maximum (2) the distance between these two maxima on a screen 50 cm from the slits.
questions.solution: (i) (1) Interference fringes are of equal width; diffraction fringes are not (the central one is twice as wide). Interference maxima are of equal intensity; in diffraction the intensity falls off for higher orders. (2) β = λD/d: wavelength, slit-to-screen distance and slit separation. (ii) (1) θ = λ/d = 1/100 = 0.01 rad. (2) y = Dθ = 50 × 0.01 = 0.5 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
(i) A spherical surface of radius of curvature R separates two media of refractive indices n₁ and n₂. A point object is placed in front of the surface at distance u in the medium of refractive index n₁ and its image is formed at distance v in the medium of refractive index n₂. Derive a relation between u and v.
(ii) A solid glass sphere of radius 6.0 cm has a small air bubble trapped at a distance 3.0 cm from its centre C, on the side nearer the observer. The refractive index of the glass is 1.5. Find the apparent position of the bubble when seen through the nearer surface of the sphere from a point outside in air.
questions.solution: (i) For a ray from object O making small angles with the axis, with the normal through the centre of curvature: i = α + γ and r = γ − β; Snell's law for small angles gives n₁i = n₂r. With α ≈ MN/OM, β ≈ MN/MI, γ ≈ MN/MC and the sign convention, n₂/v − n₁/u = (n₂ − n₁)/R. (ii) Light goes from glass (n₁ = 1.5) into air (n₂ = 1). The bubble is 3 cm inside the surface: u = −3 cm, R = −6 cm. 1/v − 1.5/(−3) = (1 − 1.5)/(−6) gives 1/v = 1/12 − 1/2 = −5/12, v = −2.4 cm. The bubble appears 2.4 cm inside the surface (3.6 cm from the centre).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
A circuit: a cell of emf E = 6.0 V and internal resistance r = 1.0 Ω is connected between points a (top) and h (bottom). The top wire runs a–b–c and the bottom wire h–g–f. Between b and g is a branch containing R₁ = 10 Ω (with points i and j just above and below it). Between c and f is a branch containing R₂ = 5.0 Ω (c to d) and R₃ = 5.0 Ω (e to f), with d and e joined by a wire. The currents and potential differences can be found using Kirchhoff's rules.

Which points are at the same potential in the circuit?
questions.solution: Points joined only by wire: a, b, i and c; d and e; j, g, h and f.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
A circuit: a cell of emf E = 6.0 V and internal resistance r = 1.0 Ω is connected between points a (top) and h (bottom). The top wire runs a–b–c and the bottom wire h–g–f. Between b and g is a branch containing R₁ = 10 Ω (with points i and j just above and below it). Between c and f is a branch containing R₂ = 5.0 Ω (c to d) and R₃ = 5.0 Ω (e to f), with d and e joined by a wire. The currents and potential differences can be found using Kirchhoff's rules.

What is the current through arm bg?
questions.solution: The branches bg (10 Ω) and cf (10 Ω) are in parallel: 5 Ω. Total I = 6/(5 + 1) = 1 A, shared equally, so 0.5 A flows through bg.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
A circuit: a cell of emf E = 6.0 V and internal resistance r = 1.0 Ω is connected between points a (top) and h (bottom). The top wire runs a–b–c and the bottom wire h–g–f. Between b and g is a branch containing R₁ = 10 Ω (with points i and j just above and below it). Between c and f is a branch containing R₂ = 5.0 Ω (c to d) and R₃ = 5.0 Ω (e to f), with d and e joined by a wire. The currents and potential differences can be found using Kirchhoff's rules.

Find the potential difference across resistance R₃.
questions.solution: The current in arm cf is 0.5 A, so V = 0.5 × 5 = 2.5 V.

questions.text:
A circuit: a cell of emf E = 6.0 V and internal resistance r = 1.0 Ω is connected between points a (top) and h (bottom). The top wire runs a–b–c and the bottom wire h–g–f. Between b and g is a branch containing R₁ = 10 Ω (with points i and j just above and below it). Between c and f is a branch containing R₂ = 5.0 Ω (c to d) and R₃ = 5.0 Ω (e to f), with d and e joined by a wire. The currents and potential differences can be found using Kirchhoff's rules.

What is the power dissipated in resistance R₂?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Strontium titanate is a rare oxide, a natural mineral found in Siberia. It is used as a substitute for diamond because its refractive index and critical angle, 2.41 and 24.5°, are approximately equal to those of diamond. Even an expert jeweller is unable to tell diamond and strontium titanate apart. A ray of light is incident normally on one face (AB) of an equilateral triangular prism ABC made of strontium titanate.

Trace the path of the ray showing its passage through the prism.
questions.solution: It enters AB undeviated (normal incidence) and meets face AC at 60°, more than the critical angle 24.5°, so it is totally internally reflected. It then meets face BC normally (by the geometry of the equilateral prism) and leaves without deviation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Strontium titanate is a rare oxide, a natural mineral found in Siberia. It is used as a substitute for diamond because its refractive index and critical angle, 2.41 and 24.5°, are approximately equal to those of diamond. Even an expert jeweller is unable to tell diamond and strontium titanate apart. A ray of light is incident normally on one face (AB) of an equilateral triangular prism ABC made of strontium titanate.

Briefly explain two applications of total internal reflection.
questions.solution: Optical fibres: light is guided along a thin glass fibre by repeated total internal reflection, used in communication and endoscopy. Totally reflecting prisms bend light by 90° or 180° in periscopes and binoculars. The sparkle of diamonds is also due to it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Strontium titanate is a rare oxide, a natural mineral found in Siberia. It is used as a substitute for diamond because its refractive index and critical angle, 2.41 and 24.5°, are approximately equal to those of diamond. Even an expert jeweller is unable to tell diamond and strontium titanate apart. A ray of light is incident normally on one face (AB) of an equilateral triangular prism ABC made of strontium titanate.

Define total internal reflection of light. Give two conditions for it.
questions.solution: When light travelling in a denser medium meets the boundary with a rarer medium at an angle greater than the critical angle, it is completely reflected back into the denser medium. Conditions: light must go from denser to rarer medium, and the angle of incidence must exceed the critical angle.
